wave: CORRECTNESS/SECURITY -- the CLI argument parser conflated "flag not passed" with "flag passed but its value is missing", silently defeating the EXACT_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED safety invariant on malformed invocation
wave_title: Sixth fix this generation cycle. After closing out the graph-projection survey (Call/FunctionIdentity/FunctionSignature), pivoted to a fresh area (runtime/apps-cli) via a scoped Explore survey to avoid over-mining the two already-hardened files. The survey's single reported finding was independently re-verified against real code before any change.
priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity, with a real security consequence -- apps/cli/src/main.rs's `value()` helper is the CLI's own load-bearing argument parser, and this defect let a malformed invocation silently bypass a named, documented safety check (EXACT_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED) rather than fail loud.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to runtime/src/census, runtime/src/lib.rs, and apps/cli/src/main.rs -- areas untouched by this cycle's five prior fixes (all in adapter/src/dependency/cargo.rs and core/src/graph/engineering_graph.rs). Its single reported finding was independently re-verified before any change: read apps/cli/src/main.rs's value() helper, its --base-sha call site in the work-prepare handler, and runtime/src/lib.rs's BASE_SHA_DRIFT guard directly (not from the subagent's paraphrase), confirming the exact code shape and the exact silent-bypass consequence.
key_finding: `value(args, name) -> Option<String>` used `args.iter().position(...).and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned()`, which returns `None` both when `name` is never present in `args` AND when `name` is present but is the last token (or immediately followed by another flag) with no value after it. For every REQUIRED flag (`--root`, `--goal`, `--out` on `systemize`) this ambiguity is masked by `.ok_or("... requires --flag")?`, which still fails loud either way. But `--base-sha` on `work prepare` is genuinely optional (`Option<String>` passed straight to `runtime::prepare_work`), so a missing value there was silently treated as "the caller chose not to pin a base SHA" instead of "the caller's invocation was malformed" -- defeating runtime::prepare_work's own BASE_SHA_DRIFT check entirely. Concretely reachable via a realistic caller mistake: a shell script invoking `--base-sha "$BASE_SHA"` with `$BASE_SHA` unset or empty is word-split down to a bare `--base-sha` with nothing after it, and the tool would proceed exactly as if no base-SHA pin had been requested at all -- silently accepting `work prepare`'s result against whatever HEAD happens to be checked out, defeating the exact invariant (`EXACT_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED`, named in this project's own invariant list) this flag exists to enforce.
verification_before_acting: Read apps/cli/src/main.rs's value() helper and its --base-sha call site (work-prepare handler) directly, confirming the exact code shape reported.

Read runtime/src/lib.rs's BASE_SHA_DRIFT guard (`if let Some(expected) = expected_base_sha && expected != system.snapshot.head_sha`) directly, confirming that expected_base_sha == None genuinely skips the drift check entirely rather than defaulting to some other safe behavior.

Grepped every call site of value() in apps/cli/src/main.rs (14 total across 8 subcommands) to design a general fix rather than a narrow, --base-sha-only patch, since the same ambiguity exists at every optional-flag call site (--out, --format) with lower but real severity, and a narrow fix would leave siblings with the identical latent defect.
Confirmed no existing test in this file exercised a present-but-empty flag value for any call site before writing new ones.

design_decisions.question: Fix only the --base-sha call site, or the root cause in value() itself?
design_decisions.decision: The root cause: value() now returns Result<Option<String>, String>, returning Err(format!("{name} requires a value")) when the flag is found but has no following argument, Ok(None) when genuinely absent, Ok(Some(v)) when present with a value. All 14 call sites updated to propagate via `?`. A narrow --base-sha-only fix would have left --out (used optionally in check/graph/work-prepare) and --format with the identical latent ambiguity -- lower severity there (no safety check bypassed, just a silently-wrong fallback to stdout-only output or a slightly misleading error), but the same defect class, and this file's own established pattern this cycle (BINDS_ARGUMENT/BINDS_RESULT, IMPLEMENTED_ON, HAS_PARAMETER_TYPE/HAS_RETURN_TYPE) is to fix the general pattern once found rather than patch one instance and leave known siblings.

design_decisions.question: What error message and exit behavior for a malformed flag?
design_decisions.decision: A plain `"{name} requires a value"` string, propagated through run()'s existing Result<(), String> error path exactly like every other usage error in this file (main() prints it to stderr via eprintln! and exits with ExitCode::from(2)) -- no new error-handling mechanism, reusing the file's own existing convention.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: Every CLI flag parsed via value() now fails loud (a usage error, exit code 2) when the flag is present but its value is missing, rather than silently treating it as absent -- closing the specific bypass of EXACT_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED and the same latent ambiguity at every other optional-flag call site.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added two new tests: a_base_sha_flag_with_no_following_value_is_a_usage_error_not_a_silent_none (the exact reported scenario: `work prepare --root . --goal "fix bug" --base-sha` with base-sha as the last token) and a_root_flag_with_no_following_value_is_a_usage_error (the required-flag side, confirming a malformed --root now gets its own accurate error rather than being silently reported as "--root was never passed"). Falsified per this session's standing discipline: backed up the file, reverted value()'s internal logic to its original absent/missing-value-conflating behavior WHILE keeping the Result<Option<String>, String> signature (so all 14 call sites still compiled, isolating exactly the behavioral regression under test rather than breaking the build), ran both new tests, confirmed both failed -- the --base-sha test's failure output is itself direct proof of the exact bug: with the reverted logic, `run()` silently proceeded past the malformed --base-sha flag straight into `runtime::prepare_work` against this repository's REAL checked-out HEAD, producing "WORK_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED" (an unrelated real blocker) instead of the expected "--base-sha requires a value" usage error -- then restored the fix from backup (git diff --stat confirmed the restored file exactly matched the fix) and confirmed both tests pass.
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: cargo fmt --all --check: clean. cargo test --workspace: 547 total (293 adapter, 5 apps/cli, 171 core, 78 runtime), 0 failed -- up from 545 (+2 new tests). docs audit --root .atlas: gate_ready true. Sanity-checked a normal, well-formed invocation (`contract --format json`) still exits 0 with correct output, confirming zero regression to legitimate usage.

implementation.code_change: apps/cli/src/main.rs -- value() now returns Result<Option<String>, String>, erroring when a flag is present but has no following value instead of silently returning None. All 14 call sites updated to propagate the new Result via `?` (required-flag `.ok_or(...)` sites, optional `if let Some(...) = value(...)?` sites, and the --format equality check). Added two new tests.
implementation.docs_change: NONE -- this is a pure correctness/security fix to already-existing, already-documented CLI behavior (EXACT_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED is a pre-existing, already-documented invariant); no new architectural concept introduced.

adversarial_and_falsification_coverage: reverted value()'s internal logic (kept the Result wrapper so the build still compiled, isolating exactly the behavioral change under test) and confirmed the new test fails with output that IS the bug itself -- the malformed --base-sha flag silently let the command proceed into a real git-backed runtime::prepare_work call against this repository's actual HEAD -- before trusting the fix, using a full file backup/restore cycle

recensus_scope_after_promotion: no prior CLOSED/EXTINCT conclusion depended on the CLI silently accepting a malformed flag value, so no external conclusion requires reopening -- this only makes a previously-silent-success path fail loud instead

the same Explore survey examined runtime/src/census/mod.rs's dedup/sort/merge-key logic in detail and found no comparable defect (every merge key traced through to a construction that cannot collide content-distinct facts) -- not exhaustive of runtime/, but no further immediately-actionable gap in that specific area is currently known

any external script or CI wrapper invoking this CLI with a malformed flag (missing value) that previously silently succeeded will now see that invocation fail with a usage error -- an intentional, correct behavior change consistent with the tool's own fail-loud discipline elsewhere in this file, not a regression
overall_verdict: FIXED, FALSIFIED, AND VERIFIED. The CLI's argument parser no longer conflates a malformed flag (present but missing its value) with an absent one, closing a real, realistically-reachable silent bypass of the EXACT_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED safety invariant and the same latent ambiguity at every other optional-flag call site in the file. Falsified via a targeted behavioral revert (kept the Result signature to isolate the exact regression) whose failure output directly demonstrated the original bug reaching a real runtime::prepare_work call against this repository's own HEAD. Full workspace test suite green (547/547).
